item.research_question: To evaluate the biocompatibility of Ti-6Al-4V alloy powder by determining its effects on behavior, blood chemistry, and antioxidant profiles in vital organs of albino mice after short-term exposure.
item.material_system: Ti-6Al-4V alloy powder (6% aluminum and 4% vanadium by weight, >99.9% purity constituents)
item.processing_route: Melting in an electric arc furnace under 10−5 mbar vacuum with argon gas, repeated four times for homogeneity; homogenized at 1100 °C in vacuum for 8 h; powder prepared for gavage at 25 mg/ml solvent/Kg body weight
item.test_conditions: Oral gavage for 8 days; behavioral tests (rota rod, open field, novel object, light-dark box); analysis of complete blood count, serum parameters, and antioxidant metabolites (SOD, catalase, lipid peroxidation) in liver, heart, lungs, kidney, and brain
key_findings: Rota rod test performance significantly decreased in male mice (P = 0.05) compared to control.
Novel object recognition capability significantly reduced in female mice (P = 0.04) compared to control.
Superoxide dismutase (SOD) concentration significantly elevated in liver (P = 0.008), heart (P = 0.01), and lungs (P = 0.05) of female mice.
Catalase concentration significantly decreased in liver (P = 0.001) of female mice.
SOD concentration in lungs significantly reduced (P = 0.05) in male mice.
Body weight, complete blood count, and serum parameters remained unaffected in both genders.
Open field, light-dark box, and other antioxidant parameters varied non-significantly (P > 0.05).
item.mechanism: The alloy powder crosses the blood-brain barrier to affect brain functioning, and the observed changes in antioxidant enzymes (SOD and catalase) reflect disturbed H₂O₂ associated metabolic pathways and increased H₂O₂ production in cells due to ROS formation from metal corrosion or ion release.
item.limitations: The exposure time of 8 days may not have been long enough to disturb blood chemistry, and the study was limited to a single dose (25 mg/ml solvent/Kg body weight).
item.future_work: Effects must be extensively explored under variable dose and exposure time conditions to know more about their biocompatibility.
quotes: Short tern exposure to Ti 6Al 4V powder drastically affected neuromuscular coordination in male mice during rota rod test.

Analysis of antioxidant parameters in vital organs has demonstrated that the applied dose of Ti-6Al-4V alloy powder can disturb the H₂O₂ associated metabolic pathways in albino mice, especially in female mice.

As this alloy is part of surgical implants, so we recommend that their effects in living systems must be extensively explored under variable dose and exposure time conditions to know more about their biocompatibility.
